FastSlow
Slower
0.5 lb/wk, ~250 kcal/day: skip one small snack a day. You won't notice the difference.
Standard (Recommended)
1 lb/wk, ~500 kcal/day: cut one takeout meal a week, lighter dinners most nights.
Faster (Use Caution)
2 lb/wk, ~1,000 kcal/day: real hunger every day. Meals get smaller. Hard to keep up past a few months.

Think of fat loss like a plane landing. Steep dives are safe at altitude, but risky close to the ground. With more fat to pull from, you can run a steeper deficit and keep your muscle. As you lean out, you need to level off, or you start burning muscle instead of fat. Your body can only pull energy from fat stores so fast: about 22 calories per pound of fat you carry, per day. At your fat mass, that ceiling is about 1,250 kcal/day, above what even the aggressive pace asks for. All three paces are safe for you. It comes down to how much hunger you're willing to sit with.

1 lb of fat ≈ 3,500 calories. Weekly pace × 3,500 ÷ 7 = daily deficit required.
@asherrobinsonfitnessSource: Harvard Health, ACSM, Alpert et al.

What Moves You Forward
Do all of these, and you're more likely to reach your goal.
Nutrition
You hit your protein target: 168–210g a day (0.8–1g per lb of bodyweight).
You eat in a calorie deficit.
You eat less energy than you burn. Your body pulls the difference from stored fat.
Training
You strength train 2–4 times a week.
Three full-body days a week is the sweet spot for most people.
You add weight or reps most weeks.
This is progressive overload. It tells your body to keep the muscle you have.
Cardio / Conditioning
You do 2–3 cardio sessions a week, plus daily walking.
Cardio burns extra calories. Eat more and still lose fat, or eat the same and lose it faster.
Consistency / Habits
You log every meal, weighed or measured.
Photo-based food apps guess. Weighing your food keeps the number honest.
You weigh in daily and track the weekly average.
A single day can jump from water or salt. The weekly average shows your real trend.
You know your average daily calorie burn.
This sets your deficit. Guess it wrong, and a "deficit" can turn into a surplus.
